stem: Kabir studies a line chart of weekly rainfall for two towns. The horizontal axis is labelled week number, the vertical axis is labelled rainfall in mm, markers sit on plotted points, and a legend names a solid line as Town P and a dashed line as Town Q.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states what he must decide before reading any value or pattern?

options.text: Identify what each axis, scale, marker, line, and legend entry represents, then read values.
Read a rainfall value from a marker before the axis scales are identified.
Apply a pie-slice legend rule to these line-chart axes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Axes, scale, markers, lines, and legend fix what each plotted point means; values and patterns come after that reading.

teacher.key_rationale: Before comparing values, Kabir must map axes, scale, markers, lines, and legend. Reading a marker first omits that step. A pie-slice legend rule is outside line-chart reading.
